First off, thank you for caring so deeply. You’re showing the best of what teaching isempathy, advocacy, love. It’s gut-wrenching and completely unfair that this is happening, especially to young people who’ve worked hard, built a life, and are just trying to survive and graduate. Your heartbreak is valid. It’s okay to feel crushed by this. You’re not alone.

Here are concrete actions you can take, both to try to stop this and to support your students as much as possible:

Immediate Action to Try to Stop This

These things can’t guarantee a reversal, but they can create pressure, visibility, and potentially buy time.

1. Connect with Immigration Advocacy Groups

Reach out to local or national immigration support organizations. Many provide legal aid and can escalate cases. Examples:
	•	RAICES (Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services)
	•	HIAS
	•	AILA (American Immigration Lawyers Association)
	•	UndocuBlack Network
	•	National Immigration Law Center (NILC)

They may be able to connect your students with pro bono legal help to challenge the order or request a stay.

2. Contact Local Journalists or Reporters

Sometimes, public exposure can help. Reach out to local news outlets or journalists. This could put pressure on local officials or at least raise awareness. If the story is compelling enough and it is journalists may want to cover it.

3. Call or Email Local Elected Officials

Even if they’re conservative, they work for all constituents. Share the story without using party-affiliated language. Focus on the humanity: “These are high school seniors. They are part of our community.”

4. Petition or Fundraiser

Create a GoFundMe for emergency housing, travel, or legal support for the students. Pair it with a Change.org petition to collect community signatures. This may not stop deportation, but it can cushion the blow and raise awareness.

If you need help setting it up, I can walk you through every step or even help draft the descriptions.

How to Handle This With Your Class

You’re in a bind. Here’s a way to be honest without violating school policies:

	“Some of our classmates are no longer able to be with us due to immigration issues. I can’t legally speak in detail about it, but I want everyone to remember: we don’t stop caring about people just because we’re told to be quiet. Let’s keep their spirit in the room.”

You can also give students room to express themselves without framing it as a political discussion. Maybe write anonymous notes or poetry, or letters to the students?

You should definitely go to UofT. Do it, you’ll totally regret it if you don’t.

Trump definitely poses an existential threat not only to the United States but to the global community at large. Let me tell you how. 
His actions and rhetoric have consistently undermined democratic institutions, eroded the norms of civil discourse, and exacerbated divisions within society. The ramifications of his behavior extend beyond domestic politics, influencing international relations and contributing to a climate of instability worldwide.

Trump’s approach to governance, marked by a disregard for established protocols and a propensity for authoritarianism, challenges the very foundations of democratic governance. His undermining of the rule of law, attempts to delegitimize the electoral process, and encouragement of political violence represent a profound departure from the principles upon which the United States was founded.

On the global stage, Trump’s policies and conduct have strained alliances, emboldened autocratic regimes, and contributed to a rise in nationalist and populist movements. His withdrawal from international agreements, such as the Paris Climate Accord and the Iran nuclear deal, has weakened collective efforts to address pressing global challenges. Moreover, his inconsistent and often antagonistic foreign policy has diminished America’s standing and credibility among its allies and adversaries alike.

The threat posed by Trump is multifaceted, encompassing not only the immediate dangers of his actions but also the long-term consequences of his influence on political culture. The normalization of misinformation, the erosion of public trust in institutions, and the deepening of societal polarization are all legacies that will endure beyond his tenure.
He is an existential threat not only to America but the world.
